sections.title: DAKOTAS/ERN MT
sections.text: RICH LOW LEVEL MOISTURE WILL RETURN NWD DURING THE DAY FED INITIALLY BY A 30 KT LLJ PRIOR TO THE START OF THE PERIOD. THIS WILL OCCUR IN CONJUNCTION WITH A WARM FRONT MOVING NWD THROUGH NEB INTO SD BY AFTERNOON AS AN INVERTED SURFACE TROUGH BECOMES MORE PRONOUNCED EXTENDING NWWD FROM THE LOW INTO ERN MT AND A DRYLINE-LIKE FEATURE EXTENDING SWD INTO THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS. A HOT/DEEPLY MIXED AIRMASS NOSING UP TO THE BOUNDARY ALONG WITH INCREASING LOW LEVEL CONFLUENCE/CONVERGENCE INVOF THE BOUNDARIES SHOULD SUFFICIENTLY WEAKEN THE CAP BY LATE AFTERNOON. THE AIRMASS WILL PRE-CONDITION AND BECOME QUITE UNSTABLE WITH MLCAPE UPWARDS OF 1000-2000 J/KG IN ERN MT TO 3000+ J/KG OVER PORTIONS OF THE DAKOTAS. INCREASING MID-UPPER SWLY FLOW AND UPPER FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL SWEEP EWD FROM WRN WY-MT AND OVERSPREAD THE MOIST SECTOR BY LATE AFTERNOON INTO THE EARLY EVENING HOURS. THE SHEAR PROFILES WILL FAVOR AN INITIAL SUPERCELL MODE EARLY WITH LARGE TO VERY LARGE HAIL/DMGG WINDS POSSIBLE AND PERHAPS AN ISOLD TORNADO OR TWO. THIS SHOULD OCCUR BEFORE STORMS BECOME MORE NUMEROUS AND EVENTUALLY CONSOLIDATE INTO ONE OR MORE EWD MOVING MCS/S WITH DMGG WINDS BECOMING THE PRIMARY THREAT WITH TIME...AS TH

sections.title: MN/IA INTO THE SRN GREAT LAKES
sections.text: MODEL GUIDANCE EXUDES MORE VARIABILITY WITH REGARD TO PLACEMENT OF ONE OR MORE STORM CLUSTERS THAT MAY BE ONGOING/REINTENSIFY DURING THE DAY ACROSS THE MID MS VALLEY INTO THE SRN GREAT LAKES REGION. ANOTHER AREA FOR ISOLD STORMS MAY BE ALONG THE WARM FRONT THAT WILL BE DISPLACED FROM THE STRONGER UPPER FORCING FOR ASCENT LOCATED TO THE W. HERE...LIFT WILL TEND TO BE WEAK-NEBULOUS BEFORE INCREASING ISENTROPIC ASCENT/LOW LEVEL WARM ADVECTION OCCURS DURING THE EVENING/OVERNIGHT. NONETHELESS...MODELS SHOW AN AXIS OF STRONG POTENTIAL INSTABILITY DEVELOPING ACROSS THE CORN BELT DUE PRIMARILY TO HOT TEMPS AND RICH LOW LEVEL MOISTURE/EVAPOTRANSPORATION. DEEP SHEAR WILL REMAIN SUBJUGATED DUE TO THE PROXIMITY OF THE UPPER HIGH TO THE S WITH A MULTICELLULAR ISOLD WIND/HAIL THREAT POSSIBLE. ..SMITH/KERR/COHEN.. 07/22/2011

sections.title: MT/ND/SD
sections.text: A BROAD UPPER TROUGH OVER THE PACIFIC NORTHWEST WILL TRACK EASTWARD INTO MT/WY THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. RICH LOW LEVEL MOISTURE WILL STREAM NORTHWESTWARD AHEAD OF THE TROUGH...WITH A VERY UNSTABLE AIR MASS LIKELY TO DEVELOP FROM SOUTHEAST MT INTO THE DAKOTAS BY EVENING. DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 60S AND STEEP LOW/MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL YIELD MLCAPE VALUES OVER 4000 J/KG OVER THIS REGION. THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP OVER CENTRAL MT BY MID/LATE AFTERNOON AND SPREAD EASTWARD INTO THE DAKOTAS DURING THE EVENING. RATHER STRONG SOUTHEASTERLY LOW LEVEL FLOW SUGGESTS THE INITIAL STORMS WILL LIKELY BE SUPERCELLULAR WITH A RISK OF VERY LARGE HAIL AND A FEW TORNADOES. HOWEVER...SEVERAL MODEL SOLUTIONS SUGGEST THE POTENTIAL FOR AN ORGANIZED BOW TRACKING QUICKLY ACROSS ND AND NORTHERN SD THIS EVENING. THIS EVOLUTION WOULD INDICATE THE RISK OF A RATHER WIDESPREAD DAMAGING WIND EVENT. IF 12Z MODEL SOLUTIONS MAINTAIN THIS RISK...THE POTENTIAL EXISTS FOR AN UPGRADE TO MODERATE RISK FOR PORTIONS OF ND/SD.

sections.title: MIDWEST INTO OH VALLEY
sections.text: FARTHER SOUTHEAST...HIGH CAPE VALUES AND RICH MOISTURE WILL BE PRESENT TODAY FROM MN/IA INTO THE OH VALLEY AND MID ATLANTIC REGION. WEAK BUT SUFFICIENT MID LEVEL FLOW MAY RESULT IN A FEW STRONG TO SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON WITH LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS LIKELY TO BE THE MAIN THREAT. ..HART/HURLBUT.. 07/22/2011

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: EXTENSIVE TROPICAL RIDGE AXIS AND STAGNANT HOT AND VERY HUMID AIRMASS WILL REMAIN IN PLACE ACROSS MOST OF THE CONUS SOUTH OF ABOUT 40N AND EAST OF ABOUT 100W. THUS...PRIMARY BELT OF MID-UPPER WLY FLOW WILL REMAIN CONFINED TO THE NRN BORDER STATES AND SRN CANADA. A WELL-DEFINED SHORT WAVE TROUGH WAS EVIDENT IN WATER VAPOR IMAGERY CROSSING ID THIS MORNING AND WILL LIKELY CONTRIBUTE TO MOST OF THE SUBSTANTIAL SEVERE WEATHER DEVELOPMENT LATER TODAY FROM MT EAST ACROSS PORTIONS OF NORTH AND SOUTH DAKOTA. ELSEWHERE...FAIRLY WIDESPREAD AND DIURNALLY DRIVEN DEEP CONVECTION IS AGAIN ANTICIPATED OVER THE SRN ROCKIES...ALONG PORTIONS OF THE CNTRL GULF COAST...AND ACROSS FL. VERY WEAK SHEAR BUT HOT AND STRONGLY UNSTABLE CONDITIONS IN THESE AREAS WOULD SUPPORT SCATTERED/RANDOM AND SHORT-LIVED DOWNBURST EVENTS WITHIN A FEW HOURS EITHER SIDE OF PEAK HEATING LATER TODAY.

sections.title: MT AND WRN DAKOTAS
sections.text: AT LEAST TWO BOUNDARIES EXTEND EAST OF THE DEVELOPING MT LEE CYCLONE AND ACROSS THE NRN/CNTRL PLAINS THIS MORNING. A DEEPER SYNOPTIC FRONT EXTENDS FROM A STRONG LOW PRESSURE SYSTEM MOVING TOWARD JAMES BAY CANADA SWWD TO THE ARROWHEAD OF MN AND THEN WSWWD INTO SD WHERE IT INTERSECTS A WEAK LEE/TRIPLE-POINT LOW SOUTHEAST OF THE BLACK HILLS. THIS BOUNDARY THEN CONTINUES NWWD TO THE DEVELOPING LOW IN ERN MT. A WEAKER BOUNDARY EXISTS SOUTH OF THE SYNOPTIC FRONT...FROM THE MCS ACROSS LOWER MI AND SRN LAKE MICHIGAN WWD ACROSS THE MO RIVER VALLEY. LOW LEVEL MOISTURE TRANSPORT AND STRONG HEATING ARE UNDERWAY ACROSS ERN MT AND SHOULD LEAD TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF VERY STRONG INSTABILITY BY AFTERNOON. DEEPENING SURFACE LOW PRESSURE WILL ENHANCE LOW LEVEL ELY/UPSLOPE FLOW WHILE STRONGER MID LEVEL WINDS AND HEIGHT FALLS SPREAD EAST WITH THE SHORT WAVE TROUGH AND DEVELOPING FRONTAL CIRCULATION. STORM SCALE MODEL GUIDANCE IS IN VERY GOOD AGREEMENT THAT DEEP CONVECTION WILL FIRST INITIATE ACROSS THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF SWRN MT AND THEN NEAR THE INVERTED/ LEE TROUGH AND LOW IN THE 20-22 UTC TIME PERIOD. AN AXIS OF GREATER CAPE IS FORECAST FROM THE LEE LOW ESEWD ALONG THE FRONTAL ZONE ACROSS THE DAKOTAS

sections.title: ERN DAKOTAS/MN AND MIDDLE MO RIVER VALLEY
sections.text: CONFIDENCE IN STORM DEVELOPMENT IN THESE AREAS IS MORE UNCERTAIN GIVEN STRONG CAPPING AND WEAKER FORCING. SECONDARY/WEAKER BOUNDARY FROM MIDWEST MCS WWD ACROSS IA/NEB MAY ACT AS A FOCUS FOR DEVELOPING STORMS WHERE A SMALL MCV APPEARS TO BE SUSTAINING A CLUSTER OF WEAK TSTMS MOVING INTO WRN IA ATTM. ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT IS POSSIBLE ALONG THE SYNOPTIC FRONT FROM ERN SD INTO MN WHERE DEEP-LAYER SHEAR WOULD SUPPORT MORE PERSISTENT UPDRAFTS AND SOME POTENTIAL FOR SUPERCELLS. ONE OR TWO CONVECTIVE CLUSTERS MAY EVOLVE FROM THIS ACTIVITY LATER THIS EVENING AND POSE SOME CHANCE FOR LOCAL DAMAGING WINDS...AS WELL AS MORE HEAVY RAIN...FROM ERN NRB/SD AND SRN MN ACROSS IA.

sections.title: MIDWEST/OH VALLEY
sections.text: A VERY HOT AND UNSTABLE AIRMASS WAS DEVELOPING NORTH OF THE OH RIVER...FROM OH WWD ACROSS IND AND EXTREME LOWER MI. THIS DESTABILIZATION WAS TAKING PLACE AHEAD OF THE LAKE MICHIGAN MCS WITH LATEST DIAGNOSTIC DATA INDICATING MLCAPE VALUES IN EXCESS OF 3000 J PER KG. WHILE SHEAR WILL REMAIN MARGINAL/LIMITED FOR WIDESPREAD ORGANIZED SEVERE...THE DEGREE OF CAPE/DCAPE...WHEN COMBINED WITH CONTINUED HEATING AND THE APPROACH OF MCS/MCV...WARRANTS INCREASING SEVERE WIND PROBABILITIES OVER THESE AREAS COMMENSURATE WITH A SLGT RISK. ..CARBIN/DEAN/IMY/GUYER.. 07/22/2011

sections.title: MT/DAKOTAS TO UPPER MIDWEST
sections.text: PER MID-AFTERNOON ANALYSIS/OBSERVATIONAL TRENDS...EASTWARD MOVING COLD FRONT WILL CONTINUE TO OVERTAKE AN INVERTED SURFACE TROUGH/ASSOCIATED MOIST AXIS ACROSS THE NORTHERN HIGH PLAINS. WHILE SOMEWHAT REMOVED FROM THE RICHER BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE...A SPECIAL 18Z OBSERVED FROM GLASGOW SAMPLED A HIGHLY SHEARED ENVIRONMENT IN THE PRESENCE OF STRENGTHENING FLOW ALOFT/IMPLIED DPVA CROSSING MT THIS AFTERNOON. EXPECTATIONS ARE FOR SUSTAINED SEVERE STORMS/SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL/POTENTIALLY SOME TORNADOES BEFORE A WIND-PRODUCING MCS EVOLVES FROM FAR EASTERN MT INTO THE DAKOTAS THROUGH TONIGHT. OTHER STRONG/SEVERE STORMS MAY ALSO FORM NEAR THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF SOUTHERN MT/NORTHERN WY LATER THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING. OTHER FOCUS AREAS FOR SEVERE TSTMS POTENTIALLY INCLUDE AHEAD OF DUAL MCV/S ACROSS IA/SOUTHERN MN...AS WELL AS ALONG THE SURFACE FRONT/INSTABILITY AXIS ACROSS SD/SOUTHERN ND LATER THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING. SEE MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 1690...AS WELL AS SUBSEQUENT MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS/POTENTIAL WATCHES FOR THESE REGIONS.

sections.title: MIDWEST/UPPER OH VALLEY
sections.text: HAVE MADE MODEST SPATIAL ADJUSTMENTS TO THE SLIGHT RISK TO ACCOUNT FOR CONTINUED MCV/COLD POOL-AIDED STRONG/SEVERE TSTM DEVELOPMENT INTO A HOT/VERY UNSTABLE AIRMASS ACROSS THE REGION. PRIMARY THREAT WILL REMAIN DOWNBURSTS/WIND DAMAGE. ..GUYER.. 07/22/2011 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1125 AM CDT FRI JUL 22 2011/

sections.title: NORTHERN PLAINS INTO PARTS OF THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY
sections.text: MODERATE RISK SEVERE PROBABILITIES HAVE BEEN MAINTAINED FOR THIS EVENING...MAINLY ACROSS PORTIONS OF WEST CENTRAL AND SOUTHWEST NORTH DAKOTA. A SIGNIFICANT MESOSCALE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM CONTINUES TO EVOLVE BENEATH DIVERGENT UPPER FLOW ACROSS THE HIGH PLAINS...DOWNSTREAM OF A VIGOROUS SHORT WAVE TROUGH...NOW LIFTING THROUGH THE MONTANA/CANADIAN BORDER AREA. ALTHOUGH STRONGEST FORCING FOR UPWARD VERTICAL MOTION MAY BEGIN TO WEAKEN SHORTLY...AND DEEP LAYER WESTERLY MEAN FLOW FIELDS MAY REMAIN RATHER WEAK ACROSS MUCH OF NORTH DAKOTA...MODERATE EASTERLY LOW-LEVEL FLOW /30-40+ KT AT 850 MB/ IS ENHANCING VERTICAL SHEAR AND LOW-LEVEL SYSTEM RELATIVE INFLOW. IN THE PRESENCE OF THERMODYNAMIC PROFILES CHARACTERIZED BY MODESTLY STEEP LAPSE RATES AND SIZABLE LOW/MID-LEVEL TEMPERATURE/DEW POINT SPREADS...POTENTIAL FOR RELATIVELY WIDESPREAD STRONG DAMAGING WIND GUSTS APPEARS TO EXIST ACROSS WESTERN NORTH DAKOTA INTO THE 03-06Z TIME FRAME. ACTIVITY COULD APPROACH AREAS WEST/NORTHWEST OF BISMARCK BEFORE SLOWLY WANING OVERNIGHT. ADDITIONAL STRONG/SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT APPEARS POSSIBLE TONIGHT WITHIN ZONES OF ENHANCED DOWNSTREAM WARM ADVECTION ACROSS THE REMAINDER OF THE DAKOTAS...AND EAST OF THE MI

sections.title: PARTS OF THE UPPER OHIO VALLEY AND CENTRAL APPALACHIANS
sections.text: MERGING OUTFLOWS HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO RECENT STRONG/SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT...BUT THIS FORCING AND ASSOCIATED CONVECTION PROBABLY WILL BEGIN TO WEAKEN BY THE 02-04Z TIME FRAME. ..KERR.. 07/23/2011
